contexts.text: I spoke with one (the czar), saying that they had nothing in the other life...
I heard one (of the Russians) saying that they fear the czar, and that the czar is everywhere.

I saw the czar Peter, and spoke with him in a dream. He afterwards appeared among the Russians... who believe that he has power over their lives and possessions... I heard them together with the czar, who said that everything of theirs was his, because the region was his: but I replied that their possessions are not his, but theirs, and that he has no right over their lives, but that they would give of their property so much as was necessary for the safety of the kingdom, and no more; and that their life is from the Lord; and that they are under the law, and the czar too is under it. But it was shown that when the czar wants to have all their property, they give it to him. They worship him as their god. SE 5963.
The Papists sent two emissaries to the czar Peter the Muscovite, who knew how to insinuate themselves into his passions.
